title: Mahindra Manulife seeks Form R1 from IRDAI, builds senior team for life insurance entry- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: The insurer is also drawing senior talent from existing life insurance companies, with several executives from Bandhan Life, such as COO Jitin Parekh, understood to have moved   September 08, 2026 / 17:25 IST             Mahindra Manulife Insurance Limited has applied to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) for the issuance of Form R1, people familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol, advancing its application to enter India’s life insurance market. The filing comes as the 50:50 venture between Mahindra & Mahindra and Manulife builds the management team that will run the insurer, subject to regulatory approvals. What the R1 filing means Under IRDAI’s registration process, an applicant first obtains a no-objection certificate and then applies to the regulator for the issuance of Form R1. If IRDAI accepts the request, it issues Form R1, which remains valid for three months. The applicant must complete and submit the form within this period. The regulator can extend the validity by another three months. IRDAI then examines the promoters’ track record and financial strength, capital structure, funding sources, shareholding, planned infrastructure and five-year business plan. If the completed application receives R1 approval, the regulator issues Form R2. After examining the R2 application, IRDAI may grant the certificate of registration in Form R3. Senior team takes shape Mahindra & Mahindra and Manulife in February named Suresh Agarwal as managing director and chief executive officer-designate of the venture, subject to regulatory approvals. Agarwal had been managing director and chief executive officer of Mahindra Insurance Brokers since September 2025. He stepped down from that position on April 30 to take up the new role. He previously helped expand Kotak’s life insurance business and later led Kotak General Insurance through its transition into a joint venture with Zurich Insurance. Mahindra Manulife has also recruited executives from Bandhan Life, people familiar with the matter said. Jitin Parekh, who spent more than 16 years at Bandhan Life in roles spanning legal, compliance, secretarial and enterprise functions, has joined the new insurer. Parekh confirmed the move in a LinkedIn post, although his designation has not been publicly disclosed. People familiar with the appointments said other recruits from Bandhan Life would work across areas including technology governance and operations. Kiran Belsekar has joined Mahindra Manulife as head of technology governance after more than six years at Bandhan Life. His previous responsibilities included technology, cybersecurity, data privacy and IT governance. Mahindra & Mahindra declined to comment on the R1 filing and the appointments. Emails sent to Manulife did not elicit a response until publication. Parekh did not respond to a request for details about his role. Up to Rs 7,200 crore investment planned Mahindra Manulife Insurance Limited was incorporated in June 2026 after receiving approval from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. It is owned equally by Mahindra & Mahindra and Manulife Holdings (Bermuda) Limited. The companies announced the partnership in November 2025, marking Mahindra’s proposed entry into the life insurance business. Each partner has committed to invest up to Rs 3,600 crore over 10 years, taking the potential combined investment to Rs 7,200 crore. They expect to invest Rs 1,250 crore each during the first five years. The partners have said the insurer will offer long-term savings and protection products. It plans to use Mahindra’s distribution reach in rural and semi-urban markets and Manulife’s product, underwriting and agency capabilities, while also targeting protection products for urban customers. Mahindra Manulife must now receive Form R1, submit the completed application, secure R1 and R2 approvals, and obtain its certificate of registration before it can begin life insurance operations. September 08, 2026 / 17:25 IST

Mahindra Manulife Insurance Limited has applied to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) for the issuance of Form R1, people familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol, advancing its application to enter India’s life insurance market.

The filing comes as the 50:50 venture between Mahindra & Mahindra and Manulife builds the management team that will run the insurer, subject to regulatory approvals.

What the R1 filing means

Under IRDAI’s registration process, an applicant first obtains a no-objection certificate and then applies to the regulator for the issuance of Form R1.

If IRDAI accepts the request, it issues Form R1, which remains valid for three months. The applicant must complete and submit the form within this period. The regulator can extend the validity by another three months.

IRDAI then examines the promoters’ track record and financial strength, capital structure, funding sources, shareholding, planned infrastructure and five-year business plan.

If the completed application receives R1 approval, the regulator issues Form R2. After examining the R2 application, IRDAI may grant the certificate of registration in Form R3.

Senior team takes shape

Mahindra & Mahindra and Manulife in February named Suresh Agarwal as managing director and chief executive officer-designate of the venture, subject to regulatory approvals.

Agarwal had been managing director and chief executive officer of Mahindra Insurance Brokers since September 2025. He stepped down from that position on April 30 to take up the new role.

He previously helped expand Kotak’s life insurance business and later led Kotak General Insurance through its transition into a joint venture with Zurich Insurance.

Mahindra Manulife has also recruited executives from Bandhan Life, people familiar with the matter said.

Jitin Parekh, who spent more than 16 years at Bandhan Life in roles spanning legal, compliance, secretarial and enterprise functions, has joined the new insurer. Parekh confirmed the move in a LinkedIn post, although his designation has not been publicly disclosed.

People familiar with the appointments said other recruits from Bandhan Life would work across areas including technology governance and operations.

Kiran Belsekar has joined Mahindra Manulife as head of technology governance after more than six years at Bandhan Life. His previous responsibilities included technology, cybersecurity, data privacy and IT governance.

Mahindra & Mahindra declined to comment on the R1 filing and the appointments. Emails sent to Manulife did not elicit a response until publication. Parekh did not respond to a request for details about his role.

Up to Rs 7,200 crore investment planned

Mahindra Manulife Insurance Limited was incorporated in June 2026 after receiving approval from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. It is owned equally by Mahindra & Mahindra and Manulife Holdings (Bermuda) Limited.

The companies announced the partnership in November 2025, marking Mahindra’s proposed entry into the life insurance business.

Each partner has committed to invest up to Rs 3,600 crore over 10 years, taking the potential combined investment to Rs 7,200 crore. They expect to invest Rs 1,250 crore each during the first five years.

The partners have said the insurer will offer long-term savings and protection products. It plans to use Mahindra’s distribution reach in rural and semi-urban markets and Manulife’s product, underwriting and agency capabilities, while also targeting protection products for urban customers.

Mahindra Manulife must now receive Form R1, submit the completed application, secure R1 and R2 approvals, and obtain its certificate of registration before it can begin life insurance operations.
